Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.
And he went away from there, and came into his country; and his disciples went with him.
耶穌離開那裡，來到自己的家鄉；門徒也跟從他。

When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?

And when the Sabbath day had come, he was teaching in the Synagogue; and a number of people hearing him were surprised, saying, From where did this man get these things? and, What is the wisdom given to this man, and what are these works of power done by his hands?
到了安息日，他在會堂裡教訓人。眾人聽見，就甚希奇，說：「這人從哪裡有這些事呢？所賜給他的是甚麼智慧？他手所做的是何等的異能呢？
Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.
Is not this the woodworker, the son of Mary, and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were bitter against him.
這不是那木匠嗎？不是馬利亞的兒子雅各、約西、猶大、西門的長兄嗎？他妹妹們不也是在我們這裡嗎？」他們就厭棄他（厭棄他：原文是因他跌倒）。
Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”
And Jesus said to them, A prophet is nowhere without honour, but in his country, and among his relations, and in his family.
耶穌對他們說：「大凡先知，除了本地、親屬、本家之外，沒有不被人尊敬的。」
So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.
And he was unable to do any work of power there, but only to put his hands on one or two persons who were ill, and make them well.
耶穌就在那裡不得行甚麼異能，不過按手在幾個病人身上，治好他們。
And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.
And he was greatly surprised because they had no faith. And he went about the country places teaching.
他也詫異他們不信，就往周圍鄉村教訓人去了。
Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
And he gave orders to the twelve, and sent them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits;
耶穌叫了十二個門徒來，差遣他們兩個兩個地出去，也賜給他們權柄，制伏污鬼；
He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—
And he said that they were to take nothing for their journey, but a stick only; no bread, no bag, no money in their pockets;
並且囑咐他們：「行路的時候不要帶食物和口袋，腰袋裡也不要帶錢，除了柺杖以外，甚麼都不要帶；
and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.
They were to go with common shoes on their feet, and not to take two coats.
只要穿鞋，也不要穿兩件褂子」；
And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.
And he said to them, Wherever you go into a house, make that your resting-place till you go away.
又對他們說：「你們無論到何處，進了人的家，就住在那裡，直到離開那地方。
If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”
And whatever place will not take you in and will not give ear to you, when you go away, put off the dust from your feet as a witness against them.
何處的人不接待你們，不聽你們，你們離開那裡的時候，就把腳上的塵土跺下去，對他們作見證。」
So they set out and preached that the people should repent.
And they went out, preaching the need for a change of heart in men.
門徒就出去傳道，叫人悔改，
They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil.
And they sent out a number of evil spirits, and put oil on a great number who were ill, and made them well.
又趕出許多的鬼，用油抹了許多病人，治好他們。
Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
And king Herod had news of him, because his name was on the lips of all; and he said, John the Baptist has come back from the dead, and for this reason these powers are working in him.
耶穌的名聲傳揚出來。希律王聽見了，就說：「施洗的約翰從死裡復活了，所以這些異能由他裡面發出來。」
Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”
But others said, It is Elijah. And others said, It is a prophet, even like one of the prophets.
但別人說：「是以利亞。」又有人說：「是先知，正像先知中的一位。」
But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”
But Herod, when he had news of it, said, John, whom I put to death, has come back from the dead.
希律聽見卻說：「是我所斬的約翰，他復活了。」
For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound and imprisoned, on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.
For Herod himself had sent men out to take John and put him in prison, because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, whom he had taken for himself.
先是希律為他兄弟腓力的妻子希羅底的緣故，差人去拿住約翰，鎖在監裡，因為希律已經娶了那婦人。
For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”
For John said to Herod, It is wrong for you to have your brother's wife.
約翰曾對希律說：「你娶你兄弟的妻子是不合理的。」
So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she had been unable,
And Herodias was bitter against him, desiring to put him to death; but she was not able;
於是希羅底懷恨他，想要殺他，只是不能；
because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. When he heard John’s words, he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.
For Herod was in fear of John, being conscious that he was an upright and holy man, and kept him safe. And hearing him, he was much troubled; and he gave ear to him gladly.
因為希律知道約翰是義人，是聖人，所以敬畏他，保護他，聽他講論，就多照著行（有古卷：游移不定），並且樂意聽他。
On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
And the chance came when Herod on his birthday gave a feast to his lords, and the high captains, and the chief men of Galilee;
有一天，恰巧是希律的生日，希律擺設筵席，請了大臣和千夫長，並加利利作首領的。
When the daughter of Herodias came and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests, and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”

And when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and did a dance, Herod and those who were at table with him were pleased with her; and the king said to the girl, Make a request for anything and I will give it you.
希羅底的女兒進來跳舞，使希律和同席的人都歡喜。王就對女子說：「你隨意向我求甚麼，我必給你。」
And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”
And he took an oath, saying to her, Whatever is your desire I will give it to you, even half of my kingdom.
又對她起誓說：「隨你向我求甚麼，就是我國的一半，我也必給你。」
Then she went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?” And her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist.”
And she went out and said to her mother, What is my request to be? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
她就出去對她母親說：「我可以求甚麼呢？」她母親說：「施洗約翰的頭。」
At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”
And she came in quickly to the king, and said, My desire is that you give me straight away on a plate the head of John the Baptist.
她就急忙進去見王，求他說：「我願王立時把施洗約翰的頭放在盤子裡給我。」
The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.
And the king was very sad; but because of his oaths, and those who were with him at table, he would not say 'No' to her.
王就甚憂愁；但因他所起的誓，又因同席的人，就不肯推辭，
So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.
And straight away the king sent out one of his armed men, and gave him an order to come back with the head: and he went and took off John's head in prison,
隨即差一個護衛兵，吩咐拿約翰的頭來。護衛兵就去，在監裡斬了約翰，
The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.
And came back with the head on a plate, and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother.
把頭放在盤子裡，拿來給女子，女子就給她母親。
When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.
And when his disciples had news of it, they came and took up his body, and put it in its last resting-place.
約翰的門徒聽見了，就來把他的屍首領去，葬在墳墓裡。
Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.
And the twelve came together to Jesus; and they gave him an account of all the things they had done, and all they had been teaching.
使徒聚集到耶穌那裡，將一切所做的事、所傳的道全告訴他。
And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
And he said to them, Come away by yourselves to a quiet place, and take a rest for a time. Because there were a great number coming and going, and they had no time even for food.
他就說：「你們來，同我暗暗地到曠野地方去歇一歇。」這是因為來往的人多，他們連吃飯也沒有工夫。
So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.
And they went away in the boat to a waste place by themselves.
他們就坐船，暗暗地往曠野地方去。
But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.
And the people saw them going, and a number of them, having knowledge who they were, went running there together on foot from all the towns, and got there before them.
眾人看見他們去，有許多認識他們的，就從各城步行，一同跑到那裡，比他們先趕到了。
When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
And he got out, and saw a great mass of people, and he had pity on them, because they were like sheep without a keeper: and he gave them teaching about a number of things.
耶穌出來，見有許多的人，就憐憫他們，因為他們如同羊沒有牧人一般，於是開口教訓他們許多道理。
By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.
And at the end of the day, his disciples came to him and said, This place is waste land, and it is late:
天已經晚了，門徒進前來，說：「這是野地，天已經晚了，
Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
Send them away, so that they may go into the country and small towns round about, and get some food for themselves.
請叫眾人散開，他們好往四面鄉村裡去，自己買甚麼吃。」
But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”
But he said to them in answer, Give them food yourselves. And they said to him, Are we to go and get bread for two hundred pence, and give it to them?
耶穌回答說：「你們給他們吃吧。」門徒說：「我們可以去買二十兩銀子的餅給他們吃嗎？」
“Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five—and two fish.”
And he said to them, How much bread have you? go and see. And when they had seen, they said, Five cakes of bread and two fishes.
耶穌說：「你們有多少餅，可以去看看。」他們知道了，就說：「五個餅，兩條魚。」
Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.
And he made them all be seated in groups on the green grass.
耶穌吩咐他們，叫眾人一幫一幫地坐在青草地上。
So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
And they were placed in groups, by hundreds and by fifties.
眾人就一排一排地坐下，有一百一排的，有五十一排的。

Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.

And he took the five cakes of bread and the two fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said words of blessing over them; and when the cakes were broken, he gave them to the disciples to put before the people; and he made division of the two fishes among them all.
耶穌拿著這五個餅，兩條魚，望著天祝福，擘開餅，遞給門徒，擺在眾人面前，也把那兩條魚分給眾人。
They all ate and were satisfied,
And they all took of the food and had enough.
他們都吃，並且吃飽了。
and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.
And they took up twelve baskets full of the broken bits and of the fishes.
門徒就把碎餅碎魚收拾起來，裝滿了十二個籃子。
And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves.
And those who took of the bread were five thousand men.
吃餅的男人共有五千。
Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.
And straight away he made his disciples get into the boat, and go before him to the other side to Beth-saida, while he himself sent the people away.
耶穌隨即催門徒上船，先渡到那邊伯賽大去，等他叫眾人散開。
After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.
And after he had sent them away, he went up into a mountain for prayer.
他既辭別了他們，就往山上去禱告。
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
And by evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he by himself on the land.
到了晚上，船在海中，耶穌獨自在岸上；
He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,

And seeing that they had trouble in getting their boat through the water, because the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea; and he would have gone past them;
看見門徒因風不順，搖櫓甚苦。夜裡約有四更天，就在海面上走，往他們那裡去，意思要走過他們去。
but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—
But they, when they saw him walking on the sea, took him for a spirit, and gave a loud cry:
但門徒看見他在海面上走，以為是鬼怪，就喊叫起來；
for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
For they all saw him, and were troubled. But straight away he said to them, Take heart, it is I, have no fear.
因為他們都看見了他，且甚驚慌。耶穌連忙對他們說：「你們放心！是我，不要怕！」
Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded,
And he went to them into the boat, and the wind went down, and they were full of wonder in themselves;
於是到他們那裡，上了船，風就住了；他們心裡十分驚奇。
for they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts had been hardened.
For it was not clear to them about the bread; but their hearts were hard.
這是因為他們不明白那分餅的事，心裡還是愚頑。
When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and moored the boat.
And when they had gone across, they came to Gennesaret, and got their boat to land.
既渡過去，來到革尼撒勒地方，就靠了岸，
As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus
And when they had got out of the boat, the people quickly had news of him,
一下船，眾人認得是耶穌，
and ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
And went running through all the country round about, and took on their beds those who were ill, to where it was said that he was.
就跑遍那一帶地方，聽見他在何處，便將有病的人用褥子抬到那裡。
And wherever He went—villages and towns and countrysides—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.

And wherever he went, into small towns, or great towns, or into the country, they took those who were ill into the market-places, requesting him that they might put their hands even on the edge of his robe: and all those who did so were made well.
凡耶穌所到的地方，或村中，或城裡，或鄉間，他們都將病人放在街市上，求耶穌只容他們摸他的衣裳繸子；凡摸著的人就都好了。
